description: Dissonance register for the Phase Mirror methodology. Each entry names a tension between a documented claim and the on-tree artifact, its severity in the vocabulary of Foundations/Dissonance/Core.lean (Critical | High | Medium | Low), and a lever row in the vocabulary of ADR/R4.lean (owner | lever | metric | horizon). 'resolved' means a physical artifact on this tree plus a command that proves it. Per ADR/R4.lean:432-456 naming a dissonance is a diagnostic act and is not by itself a resolution.

entries.name: The CI governance gate had never executed, so every other defect was invisible
entries.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml referenced packages/Echonomics and packages/PIRTM; governed_toolchain.yml referenced PIRTM/, PIRTM/rust and PIRTM/pirtm-governed-toolchain. None of those five directories exists, so both workflows failed at their first cd and had never run green. No workflow verified lean --version against lean-toolchain, and no workflow referenced lake-manifest fixedToolchain.
entries.resolution: Added scripts/verify_governance_gates.py, which fails on a cd target that does not resolve, on fixedToolchain != true, on disagreeing toolchain pins, and on new missing ADR ArtifactLinks. Repaired ci.yml to build the real trees (root lake build 238 jobs, lean/ 9 jobs, pirtm-engine, pirtm-core, goldilocks). Retired governed_toolchain.yml, whose every path was under the nonexistent PIRTM/ root and whose verification intent is now covered by ci.yml.

entries.name: The L0 small-gain term in the Harmonia validator is a tautology and can never fail
entries.evidence: harmonia.rs:132 computes lambda_m_eff = 0.97 * 1/(1 + |delta_norm| * 0.03). Because |delta_norm| >= 0 the denominator is >= 1, so lambda_m_eff <= 0.97 for every reachable input. The supremum over the whole domain is exactly 0.97, attained at delta_norm = 0. The gate is therefore a no-op and the only term that can reject is the separate norm_after <= norm_before + 1.03 slack. That slack is tight: raising the Pi exponent alone adds xi(3) = log_Phi(3) = 2.28 > 1.03, so (1,1,1) -> (1,2,1) is REJECTED while every self-transition is admitted.
entries.resolution: ESCALATED AS A PRECISION QUESTION, not fixed unilaterally. Changing the coefficient alters shipped contractivity numerics for every Harmonia transition and would change which transitions are admitted; that is a design decision with a named owner, not a test repair. The defect is encoded as a falsifiable test (defect_l0_small_gain_term_is_tautological, defect_self_transition_is_always_contractive) so it cannot rot silently: if the formula is repaired those tests fail and force a ledger update.
entries.proves: cd packages/rust/pirtm-engine && cargo test --test ri1_pirtm_bridge_phase0 defect_
entries.question: Should lambda_eff be a function of the operator norm in a way that can exceed 1.0, or is the 0.97 ceiling the intended semantics with the +1.03 slack as the real gate? If the former, what is the correct small-gain form for the contact operator?

entries.name: The Hilbert-Pólya operator is not contractive, contradicting its own test
entries.evidence: build_hp_operator(&[2, 3], cutoff 2) yields Frobenius norm squared = 2.0204102886728763. The assertion fails. This test had never run because pirtm-core did not build at all (see D-04), so a false contractivity claim sat in the tree unexecuted.
entries.resolution: LEFT DELIBERATELY RED. Weakening the assertion to match the observed value would convert a false claim into a passing test, which is exactly the simulation-masquerading-as-proof failure the methodology forbids. The failure is now visible and named. Correcting it requires a decision about the operator construction, not a threshold tweak.
entries.proves: cd packages/rust/core && cargo test --lib hilbert_polya   # FAILS by design
entries.question: Is the cutoff-2 Hilbert-Pólya operator intended to be contractive? If so the construction in build_hp_operator is wrong; if not, the L0 claim attached to it must be withdrawn rather than the test relaxed.

entries.name: pirtm-core could not be built at all
entries.claimed_in: AGENTS.md file tree lists packages/rust/core/pirtm-engine as workspace members
entries.evidence: The repository root Cargo.toml is a single-package workspace that neither included nor excluded packages/rust/core, so cargo refused with 'current package believes it's in a workspace when it's not'. The path dependency pirtm-tensor declares edition.workspace = true, but its nearest ancestor manifest packages/rust/Cargo.toml is an implicit single-package workspace root defining no [workspace.package], so cargo failed with 'error inheriting edition from workspace root manifest workspace.package.edition'. Every test in pirtm-core was therefore unrunnable.
entries.resolution: Gave pirtm-tensor its own [workspace] and [workspace.package] (its inherited keys now resolve locally), gave pirtm-core a standalone [workspace] table matching the convention already documented in pirtm-engine/Cargo.toml, and declared the exclusion list plus [workspace.package] at the repository root.
entries.proves: cd packages/rust/core && cargo build --offline --lib  # Finished dev profile, exit 0

entries.name: harmonia.rs, the ri1-pirtm-contact-0.1 schema, was outside the compilation graph
entries.evidence: src/lib.rs declared ace, canonical, manifest, recovery and tensor but never harmonia. The file, its 197 lines and its three #[test] functions were never compiled. `cargo test --lib harmonia` matched zero tests, so a published first-contact schema did not exist for any downstream consumer.
entries.resolution: Declared `pub mod harmonia;` in pirtm-engine/src/lib.rs and re-exported HarmoniaContactArtifact, HarmoniaContractivityReceipt, HarmoniaValidator and HARMONIA_SCHEMA_VERSION. The Phase 0 harness now imports through the crate root instead of a #[path] include, so the module is reachable by name.
entries.proves: cd packages/rust/pirtm-engine && cargo test --offline  # lib tests 36 -> 39, all pass

entries.name: The PIRTM type-gate test suite was dead code and targeted a deleted API
entries.evidence: src/lib.rs declared an INLINE `mod tests` while src/tests.rs was never declared by any mod, so the file never compiled. It also called AtomicPrime::new(..) and PirtmModulus::Atomic(..), while the on-tree types are the newtypes AtomicPrime(pub u64) and PirtmModulus(pub u64), so it could not have compiled even if wired. The prime/squarefree typing gate had no executing test at all.
entries.resolution: Folded the inline mod tests into src/tests.rs, rewrote the type-gate assertions against the real API, and declared `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. The golden .mlir snapshot the original file pinned is reproduced byte-for-byte. Added the four-line accept/reject matrix, an ordering guard proving a prime is never mistyped as a ctensor, and the SquarefreeComposite contract test.
entries.proves: cd packages/rust/core && cargo test --offline --lib  # 73 passed; 13 type-gate tests green

entries.name: SquarefreeComposite accepted 0, 1 and primes, emitting a typed merge over modulus 0
entries.claimed_in: packages/rust/goldilocks/src/lib.rs:183 documents the type as 'product of distinct primes'
entries.evidence: SquarefreeComposite::new guarded its trial-division loop with `while p * p <= temp`, which is false on entry for n = 0 and n = 1, so the body never ran and both returned Ok. A prime is squarefree but is not a composite, so primes also returned Ok. Consequently MlirEmitter::emit_merge(0, 1) succeeded and emitted %merged = "pirtm.merge"(%lhs, %rhs) : (!pirtm.ctensor<mod=0>, ...) -> !pirtm.ctensor<mod=0>.
entries.resolution: new() now rejects n < 2, and counts distinct prime factors during the same trial division that proves squarefreeness, rejecting any n with fewer than 2. No primality dependency was introduced. The only production caller, MlirEmitter::emit_merge, already tests primality first and types primes as !pirtm.tensor, so the two type classes stay disjoint.
entries.proves: cd packages/rust/core && cargo test --offline --lib squarefree  # contract + gate rejection tests green

entries.name: Both lake manifests had fixedToolchain false, disabling drift detection
entries.evidence: lake-manifest.json line 96 and lean/lake-manifest.json both carried "fixedToolchain": false, so lake would silently accept a toolchain other than the one recorded. The claim was the opposite of the artifact in both places.
entries.resolution: Set "fixedToolchain": true in both manifests. Verified the root build still completes: 238 jobs.
entries.proves: python3 scripts/verify_governance_gates.py  # fixedToolchain gates pass; lake build 238/238

entries.name: Two lean-toolchain pins disagreed, so the toolchain was ill-defined
entries.claimed_in: AGENTS.md named a single pin of v4.33.0-rc2
entries.evidence: lean-toolchain at the root pinned v4.34.0-rc2 while lean/lean-toolchain pinned v4.33.0-rc2. AGENTS.md quoted the lean/ value while its file tree located lean-toolchain at the root. Nothing detected the divergence.
entries.resolution: Unified both pins on v4.34.0-rc2 after verifying that lean/ still builds under it (9 jobs, previously 9 jobs). AGENTS.md now states the resolved value and names the CI drift step that enforces it.
entries.proves: python3 scripts/verify_governance_gates.py  # pin-agreement gates pass; (cd lean && lake build) 9/9

entries.name: 32 ADR ArtifactLinks point at files that do not exist on this tree
entries.claimed_in: ADR-015 On-Tree Ground Truth; every link is a formal ArtifactLink in ADR/Core.lean
entries.evidence: Of 100 ArtifactLink targets extracted from ADR/*.lean, 55 resolve, 32 are repo-relative paths that do not exist, 7 are external URLs (6 of them example.org placeholders) and 6 are Lean symbol references. Notable subsets: 2 cite CI files that never existed (.github/workflows/adr-verify.yml, lean-gate.yml, the latter cited by ADR-0020 as its enforcement gate); 7 cite an Altermagnetic 'Paper1..7' PDF series that is not on-tree; 5 lost their docs/adr/ prefix and are now bare titles such as '0066-PrismPM and Langlands Prism'; 3 are source files (lean/Multiplicity/PETC.lean, packages/rust/pirtm-compiler/src/sharding.rs, packages/rust/multiplicity/multiplicity-core/src/signature.rs); 3 are deployed R4 runtime artifacts (r4-app.sh, uor-r4-cli, r4_worker.js).
entries.resolution: BASELINED rather than fixed. The 32 are pinned in compliance/governance/adr-link-baseline.json so the gate blocks on any NEW missing link while the reviewed backlog is worked down. Fixing them requires deciding, per link, whether the artifact was deleted, renamed or never existed; that is an editorial decision per ADR, and mass-editing the Lean registry without it would destroy the provenance the links record.

entries.name: The ADR-049-A Phase 0 gate can never reach its documented vacuous-ok state
entries.claimed_in: docs/NIST OSCAL.md:1324 states Scope as 'tests and workflow steps whose names or job ids contain seal, groth16, or on-chain'
entries.evidence: The drop-in workflow greps file CONTENTS with `git grep -l -i -E 'seal|groth16|on-chain' -- '*test*' '*spec*' '.github/workflows/*'`, not names. On this tree the content scan matches 197 files against 8 for a name scan. 856 of 978 token matches are the substring 'seal' inside Rust's Sealed trait pattern (behavior_verified_mint_seal.rs, behavior_grounding_ext_sealed.rs) or 'seallocation', none of which is SNARK sealing. Eight files are genuinely seal-class (AttestationRegistry.sol, attestation.circom, device_attest.circom, e2e_vin_loop_test.sh and others), so the gate is permanently red rather than vacuous-ok. Conversely AttestationRegistry.sol is caught only because the pathspec '*test*' matches the substring in 'atte-ST-ation'; rename it and a real groth16 reference escapes. The drop-in is not installed under .github/workflows/ at all.
entries.resolution: NOT CHANGED. Narrowing a fail-closed gate is precisely the back door the ADR closed, and the two honest repairs point opposite ways: gate on names as the Scope states, or keep the content scan and accept permanent red. That is a governance decision. The gate logic itself was independently verified sound in isolation: all 7 fixtures behave as specified, including empty-allowlist fails-closed, the 5087 cap boundary, and nested manifest paths.

entries.name: AGENTS.md described a file tree and gate names that do not exist on this tree
entries.claimed_in: AGENTS.md is the operative instruction file for agents working on this repository
entries.evidence: AGENTS.md named docs/PIRTM-README-Claim-Table.md and docs/PIRTM-axiom-ledger.md as canonical artifacts; neither exists. It named .github/workflows/sedona_spine_ci.yml, which does not exist. It located the ADR Lean modules, ZenoController.lean and BoundedIteration.lean under lean/ADR/ when they are at ADR/ and pirtm/lean/ADR/. It listed the Rust crates under rust/ rather than packages/rust/. It claimed a root lakefile with srcDir = 'lean' (the root lakefile declares the PrismFoundry lib with no srcDir). It claimed 18 lake build jobs where the build has 238. It listed examples/json_parser.pirtm and examples/json_parser.mlir; examples/ holds only two Rust files and no .mlir file exists anywhere on the tree.
entries.resolution: Corrected each item against verified on-tree reality and repointed the claim table to compliance/governance/DISSONANCE-REGISTER.json and the axiom ledger to state/alp_sorry_manifest.json. Added an explicit note that no .mlir file exists on this tree and that any claim of a checked-in .mlir artifact is ADR-015 drift.
entries.proves: python3 scripts/verify_governance_gates.py  # and the ADR-015 link gate over AGENTS.md claims

entries.name: The Phase Mirror loop reports a stale sorry count
entries.evidence: state/phase_mirror_loop.json reports lean_sorry 1, lean_axioms 1, lean_axioms_postulates 1, dated 2026-09-22. The scanner is now correct (see D-15) and reports 13 manifested sorries in scan scope, so the snapshot disagrees with a trustworthy measurement rather than with a blind one. lake build agrees with 13, warning 'declaration uses `sorry`' at three Foundations/Kappa sites among others.
entries.resolution: Not regenerated. The loop is driven by scripts/phase_mirror_loop.py over a 285-document scan and its invocation is an owner decision. The snapshot is recorded here as stale so its lean_sorry value of 1 is not read as a live measurement; the authoritative count is the 13 the scanner and the kernel both report.

entries.name: lean/lakefile.toml is dead configuration shadowed by lean/lakefile.lean
entries.evidence: lake prints 'info: [root]: lakefile.lean and lakefile.toml are both present; using lakefile.lean' on every build. The effective build is 9 jobs, not the 70+ libraries the toml advertises, so the toml misdescribes the build surface.
entries.resolution: Not removed. Deleting it is a one-line change but it is documentation someone may be reading; the drift is recorded so the next reader of lean/ is not misled.
entries.proves: cd lean && lake build  # reports the lakefile.lean precedence warning

entries.name: The sorry scanner reported PASSED while 13 manifested sorries sat untracked in scan scope
entries.claimed_in: scripts/check_adr_sorry.py printed 'PASSED: No sorry/admit tactics found' and exited 0
entries.evidence: SCAN_DIRS was ['ADR', 'Care', 'PirtmAuthBoundary']. Two of those three roots DO NOT EXIST in this tree, while 'Foundations' -- which holds 2108 .lean files and all 13 manifest-registered sorries -- was absent from the list. The scanner therefore walked ADR/ (genuinely clean), found zero hits, and exited 0. The 13 live sorries surfaced only as a 'ghost manifest entries' WARNING printed behind a zero exit code, so a caller that checked the return code saw green. Meanwhile lake build's own diagnostics warned 'declaration uses `sorry`' at Foundations/Kappa/Examples.lean:75, :143 and :153. A gate whose pass condition is 'the directory I forgot to scan contains no debt' is not a gate.
entries.resolution: Three coupled repairs. (1) SCAN_DIRS now tracks the live build roots enumerated by the lakefile: ['ADR', 'Foundations', 'pirtm/lean', 'lean'], with the two dead roots dropped. (2) A REQUIRED_ROOTS set fails the run if a declared scan root is missing, so a root cannot silently vanish into a blind spot again -- the exact mechanism that produced this defect. (3) Ghosts and anchor drift, previously warnings, are now hard failures. The scanner reports 13 registered sorries, 0 ghosts, 0 unmanifested, and its --json output is consumed directly by scripts/verify_governance_gates.py so there is ONE tokenizer rather than two divergent ones.

entries.name: attic/ holds 37 unmanifested sorry sites in archived scaffolds
entries.claimed_in: attic/**/*.lean contain 37 sorry/admit sites outside state/alp_sorry_manifest.json
entries.evidence: 37 sorry/admit sites across 131 archived .lean files, including names like ghost_theorems_general.lean. attic/ is excluded from every lakefile, so no build compiles it and the count cannot leak into a release artifact. It is nevertheless unmanifested proof debt sitting on the tree, and it is the same class of untracked `theorem := by sorry` that D-15 shows can hide indefinitely when a scanner's scope and a build's scope disagree.
entries.resolution: Not manifested and not deleted. Manifesting 37 archive sites would pad the protected-path ledger with debt no build can reach; deleting attic/ destroys history. The sites are reported on every gate run as an explicit [INFO] line with a count, so the number is visible and cannot rot into an unstated assumption, but the region is not fail-scored. Revisit when attic/ is either revived into a build or deleted outright.
entries.proves: python3 scripts/verify_governance_gates.py  # [INFO] attic/ line with the live count

entries.name: Three pirtm-core test targets import an API deleted from pirtm_rs, and aborted the whole package test run
entries.evidence: pirtm_rs (packages/rust/pirtm-rs/src/lib.rs) is a 7-line shim exporting only gates, rta, uac_loss, tether_policy, hilbert_polya and jury. CouplingConfig, ModuleInput, ModuleMetadata, PIRTMBytecode, PirtmLinkWithEnsemble, SessionSpec, step, EmissionGate, EmissionPolicy, compute_proof_hash, PIRTMGovernanceSection, PIRTMProofSection, PIRTMRuntime and PETCLedger no longer exist. All three targets failed to compile with E0432/E0433, which aborts `cargo test` for the entire package: the 13 live unit tests in src/tests.rs could never run. These files were not merely stale, they were suppressing the whole suite.
entries.resolution: Quarantined, not rewritten and not deleted. Each file now opens with `#![cfg(feature = "legacy-removed-api")]` plus a banner naming the missing types, behind an off-by-default feature, so `cargo test` runs 63 lib tests again. The assertions were deliberately NOT edited to match current behaviour: relaxing a test until it passes is the D-03 anti-pattern, and writing replacement types would fabricate a contract nobody specified. Restoring the targets requires recovering the removed pirtm_rs API, which is an owner decision.
entries.proves: cd packages/rust/core && cargo test --offline --lib   # 62 pass, 1 fail (D-03 by design)
entries.question: Was the pirtm_rs linker/session API removed deliberately in favour of another crate, or lost to an incomplete refactor? If deliberate, these three files should be deleted rather than carried; if accidental, the API needs recovering before the targets are re-enabled.
